Chapter Nine: The Enduring Relevance of Songlines.
The days start getting shorter, and there’s a chill in the air. Our traveler knows—his journey’s nearly over. But even as he nears the end, the lessons of the songlines stay with him. He finds himself spending time with all kinds of people—teachers, artists, rangers, parents. Each one has their own unique connection to the land and its stories.
One afternoon, he visits a school where kids are learning both English... and the languages of their ancestors. The teacher leads them in song—her voice ringing out clear and confident. Some of the children sing shyly, others belt out the words with boldness, and together, their voices blend into something beautiful. The traveler can’t help but notice how the old and the new exist side by side. Sometimes it’s a little awkward, but more often, it’s simply extraordinary.
There’s a story he hears—about a man who left home for the city. He spends years away, but one day, the pull of childhood songs and memories brings him back. Sure, some things have changed. There are new roads, new buildings. But the land? The land is still there, waiting for him. He walks the old paths, sings the songs he remembers, and suddenly... he feels like he’s right where he belongs.
The traveler starts to realize something important. Songlines aren’t just ancient history—they’re living threads, connecting people to each other and to the land itself. In a world that sometimes feels scattered or disconnected, these songs give us a sense of belonging. They help us make sense of change, and remind us where we come from.
One evening, he joins a group of young people getting ready for ceremony. There’s laughter and teasing as they practice their songs, but underneath it all, there’s a seriousness too. They know they’re carrying something precious—something that needs to be protected and renewed for the next generation.
And that’s when it truly hits him. The songlines aren’t just about remembering the past. They’re about resilience. Think about it—they’ve survived colonization, displacement, and all the pressures of modern life. They keep going because they adapt. Because those who care about them carry them forward—in their hearts and in their voices.
The traveler realizes, these songlines aren’t just an Australian thing. No matter where you go, people are looking for ways to connect—to the land, to each other, to something bigger than themselves. And that’s what songlines offer: a way to live with respect, with close attention, and with care.
As his journey comes to a close, the traveler feels genuinely hopeful. The songs are still being sung. The stories are still being told. And the land remains alive with meaning, waiting for anyone willing to truly listen.
